headline: Is Darling Ingredients' Profit Rebound And Cash Outlook Reshaping The Investment Case?

headline: IoT-Based Industrial Equipment Monitoring System
source: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering, Management & Applied Science
summary: Academic paper describing IoT sensor systems for monitoring industrial equipment using accelerometers, temperature, oil leakage, and current sensors. While general industrial application, methodology relevant to grease trap monitoring and predictive maintenance.

headline: Erving Voters to Weigh Cemetery Expansion, Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrades
summary: Erving, Massachusetts voters will decide on May 13 whether to approve a $1 million upgrade to the Erving Center Wastewater Treatment Plant, specifically updating secondary clarifiers installed in the 1970s. summary: Darling Ingredients reported Q1 2026 profitability with combined adjusted EBITDA of $406.8 million, including $151.2 million from Diamond Green Diesel, signaling a turning point driven by late-March RVO and improving renewables margins. Management highlighted the Renewable Volume Obligation as a major policy tailwind, with 2026 and 2027 annual demand requirement of 5.4 billion gallons compared with 3.35 billion gallons a year earlier.

headline: Renewable fuel from food waste: Darling Ingredients transforms agricultural waste into sustainable products
summary: Darling Ingredients positions itself as a leader in converting food waste and animal byproducts into renewable fuels and specialty products, with operations processing over 100 million metric tons of supply globally, emphasizing its role as an essential service for rendering and renewable fuel production.

headline: May 2026 Business Report—First Quarter 2026 Solid Waste Highlights
summary: Q1 2026 solid waste earnings reports from major companies show strong pricing growth and margin expansion. RNG development supported by EPA's final RVO rule and D3 RIN stabilization around $2.40–$2.50, benefiting waste and energy service operators.

headline: Electric Garbage Trucks Are The Heavy-Duty EV Story Hiding In Plain Sight
summary: Comprehensive analysis of electric refuse collection vehicle deployments, operational challenges including payload variability, charging infrastructure requirements, and real-world range performance across different waste collection scenarios and climate conditions.

headline: CES 2026: AI, Electric Fleets and the Future of Waste Management
summary: CES 2026 coverage of Oshkosh McNeilus Volterra electric vehicles with AI-enabled bin detection, contamination detection, and the HARR-E autonomous electric refuse robot with two-piece design for improved waste handling.

summary: Darling Ingredients showcased its evolution into a global leader in rendering, collagen and renewable fuels at its May 11, 2026 Investor Day. The company highlighted Diamond Green Diesel with approximately 1.2 billion gallons of renewable diesel capacity and early adoption of sustainable aviation fuel as key growth drivers.

headline: Garbage Truck Market to Reach USD 24.8 Billion by 2035 as Electric Fleets, Smart Automation, and Sustainable Waste Collection Transform Municipal Infrastructure
summary: Global garbage truck market projected to grow from USD 15.9 billion in 2025 to USD 24.8 billion by 2035. Manufacturers integrating AI-driven fleet telematics, robotic lifting systems, electric propulsion, and advanced compaction to improve collection efficiency and meet environmental regulations.

headline: WEF Winter Meeting - May 11-14, Kansas City
summary: WEF Winter Meeting in Kansas City featuring key volunteer committees and programming development for WEFTEC. Provides opportunity for water professionals to convene on biosolids management, PFAS, resource recovery, and advanced treatment technologies.

headline: Cemetery expansion, Wastewater Treatment Plant upgrades up for votes in Erving
summary: Erving, Massachusetts voters will decide on a $1 million capital project to update the secondary clarifiers at the town-owned Erving Center Wastewater Treatment Plant, which were installed in the 1970s. The town contracts with Erving Industries Inc. to operate the plant under a cost-sharing agreement.

headline: Barrel Energy Inc. Announces Full SEC Reporting Status
summary: Barrel Energy Inc. (OTC: BRLL) announced that the Company is now a fully reporting company with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), marking a major turning point in the Company's growth strategy and public market development. Barrel Energy is a diversified energy company focused on renewable energy and nutritional energy initiatives, seeking to leverage strategic acquisitions and innovative energy solutions to create long term shareholder value.

headline: Darling Ingredients Investors Back All Proposals at Annual Meeting
summary: Darling Ingredients stockholders approved all proposals at their 2026 Annual Meeting, including election of directors and ratification of auditors. The company is a global leader in converting bio-nutrient streams into renewable fuels and sustainable products, with significant operations in rendered animal fats and used cooking oil conversion.

headline: Top Electric & CNG Garbage Trucks for Fleet Managers (2026)
summary: The 2026 refuse truck market is the first year in history where electric and natural gas options compete directly with diesel on cost, range, and operational fitness for waste collection routes, with analysis of Mack LR Electric, Peterbilt 520EV, and other alternatives.

headline: New Way and Hyzon Unveil North America's First Hydrogen Fuel Cell Refuse Truck at WasteExpo
summary: New Way Trucks and Hyzon unveiled North America's first hydrogen fuel cell-powered electric refuse truck at WasteExpo. Following February joint development agreement, the truck will test on California routes with Recology starting after the show.

headline: Notice of Lodging of Proposed Consent Decree Under the Clean Water Act
summary: DOJ lodged a proposed Consent Decree with the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts resolving alleged Clean Water Act violations stemming from discharge of oily bilge water into Fairhaven Harbor, Massachusetts. The decree requires a $200,000 civil penalty.

headline: Austin Water Breaks Ground on $1.5 Billion Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant Expansion
summary: Austin Water and City leaders broke ground on a $1.5 billion expansion of the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant, increasing capacity from 75 to 100 MGD. The project includes advanced treatment technology, UV disinfection system replacement of chlorine gas, advanced odor control with biofilters, and a flood wall. This addresses future growth projected to reach 1.5 million residents by 2040.

headline: Notice of Lodging of Proposed Consent Decree Under the Clean Water Act—Fishing Vessel Bilge Water Discharge
summary: DOJ lodged a consent decree resolving alleged Clean Water Act violations involving discharge of oily bilge water from the fishing vessel Amelia Joyce into Fairhaven Harbor. Defendant required to pay $200,000 civil penalty for failures in pollution control equipment.

headline: eCFR Title 40 Part 403 Updated — General Pretreatment Regulations for Existing and New Sources of Pollution
summary: Title 40 CFR Part 403 was last amended on May 7, 2026, containing federal general pretreatment regulations that govern industrial and commercial wastewater discharges to publicly owned treatment works (POTWs). This update affects municipal FOG enforcement programs nationwide.

headline: Oil crisis could boost struggling sustainable aviation fuel industry
summary: Article discusses how geopolitical tensions affecting global oil prices may accelerate SAF adoption by narrowing cost gaps with conventional jet fuel. Notes that used cooking oil remains the dominant feedstock for HEFA SAF production but faces feedstock scarcity challenges beyond 2030.

headline: Waste Reduction Strategies Reshape Environmental Growth
summary: Brightpath Associates released insights on how advanced analytics is transforming waste management solutions across the environmental industry. Organizations are using data-driven strategies, automation, and AI-driven monitoring systems to optimize waste reduction while supporting regulatory compliance and environmental sustainability objectives.

headline: Reno City Council Moves Forward with Sewer Fee Increase
summary: The Reno City Council voted to adopt an ordinance implementing a sewer user fee increase to support wastewater infrastructure operations and capital improvements.

headline: CDL Driver Shortage Peaks at 80,000: Wage Growth and Retention Challenges in 2026
summary: According to the American Trucking Associations and American Transportation Research Institute, the shortage of CDL drivers has stalled at a critical mark of 80,000 people. The average truck driver salary in the USA in 2026 stands at approximately $58,000–$62,000 per year, with consistent upward movement driven by chronic driver shortages and competitive pressure among carriers.

headline: Clean Harbors Announces First-Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Clean Harbors posted record Q1 2026 revenue of $1.46 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $247.9 million (up 6%), generating EPS of $1.19. summary: Clean Harbors reported better-than-expected first-quarter results with higher profitability in both operating segments, and the Environmental Services segment delivered its 16th consecutive quarter of year-over-year Adjusted EBITDA margin improvement. First-quarter revenue rose 2% to $1.46 billion and adjusted EBITDA increased 6% to $248 million, with the company lifting its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $1.24 billion-$1.30 billion.

headline: Cooking Oil Management Market Outlook 2026-2034: Growing ESG Focus on Foodservice Waste Recycling
summary: Market research identifies stringent FOG regulations in North America and Europe, with demand for automated oil management solutions surging. The cooking oil management market is projected to grow from $4.90B in 2026 to $7.13B by 2034, driven by circular economy goals and sustainability compliance mandates.

headline: Clean Harbors Q1 2026 Earnings: Record Revenue and Raised Full-Year Guidance
summary: Clean Harbors reported record Q1 2026 revenue of $1.459 billion with net income of $63.2 million and EPS of $1.19, beating analyst expectations. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $247.9 million with a 60 basis point margin expansion to 17.0%, driven by strong environmental services performance and higher base oil pricing. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.24-1.30 billion.

headline: Clean Harbors Q1 2026 Results: 16th Consecutive Quarter of ES Margin Improvement
summary: Clean Harbors' Environmental Services segment delivered its 16th consecutive quarter of year-over-year adjusted EBITDA margin improvement, with field services revenue growing 7% as emergency response and PFAS-related business expanded. The company generated over $120 million in PFAS-related revenue in 2025 with expected 2026 growth in the 25-35% range.

headline: Marine Grease Traps: How Vessels Manage FOG
summary: Article discusses FOG management onboard ships, comparing traditional passive grease traps with newer automatic grease removal systems like Marine Guardian AutoSkim. Focuses on continuous separation and removal technologies for vessel wastewater management.

headline: Clean Harbors Safety-Kleen Segment Drives Q1 Profitability with Higher Charge-for-Oil Pricing
summary: Clean Harbors Safety-Kleen Sustainable Solutions segment reported adjusted EBITDA increase of 17% to $33M despite lower revenue, driven by higher charge-for-oil pricing and improved base oil prices. The company collected 53M gallons of waste oil in Q1, maintaining strong re-refinery utilization. PFAS-related business highlighted as growing 25-35% in 2026 vs. prior 20% growth rate.

headline: Waste Collection Route Optimization: Beyond GPS Tracking
summary: Analysis of AI-powered waste collection route optimization emphasizing demand-responsive collection models, real-time fill-level monitoring, and predictive routing that adapts to dynamic waste generation patterns and prevents costly emergency dispatches.

headline: Darling Ingredients Reports Q1 2026 Results with Net Income of $134.3M and EPS of $0.83
summary: Darling Ingredients reported Q1 2026 net income of $134.3 million or $0.83 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $26.2 million, or $0.16 per diluted share, for Q1 2025. The company reported total net sales of $1.6 billion for Q1 2026, compared with $1.4 billion for the same period a year ago.

headline: Clean Harbors Announces First-Quarter 2026 Financial Results, Raises Full-Year Guidance
summary: Clean Harbors announced better-than-expected Q1 2026 results with higher profitability in both operating segments as an environmental and industrial services company. First-quarter revenue rose 2% to $1.46 billion, adjusted EBITDA increased 6% to $248 million, and the company lifted its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $1.24 billion-$1.30 billion.

summary: Environmental Services segment posted its 16th straight quarter of year-over-year margin improvement and 18th consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth. Safety-Kleen Sustainable Solutions benefited from higher charge-for-oil pricing and improving base oil prices, with adjusted EBITDA rising 17% to $33 million.

headline: Used Cooking Oil Prices Rise in Q4 2025, Driven by Biofuel Demand and Policy Support
summary: In the United States, the Used Cooking Oil (UCO) Price Index rose quarter-over-quarter in Q4 2025, driven by robust biofuel demand and rising operational costs. UCO demand outlook strengthened in Q4 2025 due to federal biofuel incentives, with retail sales increased 3.3% year-over-year in November 2025, boosting UCO generation from food service.

summary: San Antonio River Authority completed a $7.2 million design-build wastewater treatment expansion project that increased capacity from 3.96 MGD to 7.33 MGD for three Texas municipalities. The project was executed on a highly constrained site with innovative construction strategies.

summary: Darling Ingredients reported first-quarter 2026 results with sales of $1.55 billion and net income of $134.3 million, reversing a prior-year loss. summary: Darling Ingredients reported Q1 2026 net income of $134.3 million with EPS of $0.83, beating analyst expectations of $0.59 by 40.68%, though revenue of $1.55 billion slightly missed the $1.56 billion forecast. summary: Darling Ingredients reported Q1 2026 EPS of $0.83, significantly surpassing analyst expectations of $0.59 (41% beat). Revenue slightly missed at $1.55B vs. forecast $1.56B. FY2026 guidance includes revenue of approximately $6.54B and Q2 core ingredients EBITDA of $260-275M.

summary: GFL Environmental highlighted record Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin of 29.1%, up 180 basis points YoY. summary: GFL Environmental reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.64 billion (up 5.4%), with Adjusted EBITDA increasing 12.3% to $478.5 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 29.1%, the highest Q1 margin in company history with 180 basis points increase year-over-year.

headline: GFL Environmental Reports First Quarter 2026 Results and Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance
summary: GFL Environmental reported record Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin of 29.1%, a 180 basis point increase year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $478.5 million (up 12.3%). Revenue grew 8.5% organically with strong 7.0% pricing. The company completed eight acquisitions year-to-date and raised full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $90 million to approximately $2,230 million.

headline: Roanoke's CDL driver shortage causes recycling backlog — city turns to art contest for creative solution
summary: Roanoke is experiencing recycling delays due to a shortage of CDL-certified drivers, causing overflowing bins and resident frustration. The city is implementing staff augmentation efforts and weekend work schedules to address the labor shortage impact on waste collection operations.

headline: GFL Environmental Announces Proposed Acquisition of Secure Waste Infrastructure in Western Canada
summary: GFL announced a proposed acquisition of Secure Waste Infrastructure to strengthen its operations in Western Canada. Operational cost and revenue synergies are expected to be material and could represent an incremental 25 to 50 million of opportunity above 25 million of largely SGA cost savings already identified, with Secure's 2026 revenue expected to be 1.5 to 1.6 billion.

headline: GFL Environmental Q1 2026 Earnings Call: Record Margins and Eight Acquisitions Completed
summary: GFL Environmental achieved the highest adjusted EBITDA margin in company history at 29.1%, with pricing growing 7.0% and organic growth of 4.6% in Q1 2026. headline: GFL Environmental Completes Eight Acquisitions Including Frontier Waste Solutions; Raises 2026 Guidance
summary: GFL Environmental completed eight acquisitions year-to-date, including Frontier Waste Solutions in Texas. These deals add $425-450M in annualized revenue and further densify GFL's North American network. Proposed SECURE Waste acquisition expected in H2 2026 is described as incremental to current outlook. headline: GFL Environmental Reports Q1 2026 Results with Record EBITDA Margin of 29.1%
summary: GFL Environmental achieved an adjusted EBITDA margin of 29.1%, the highest Q1 margin in the company's history and a 180 basis point increase over the prior year period. The company completed eight acquisitions year-to-date, including Frontier Waste Solutions, and announced a proposed acquisition of Secure Waste Infrastructure to strengthen operations in Western Canada.

headline: EPA Updates Interim PFAS Destruction and Disposal Guidance
summary: The EPA released updated Interim Guidance on PFAS destruction and disposal published in the Federal Register on April 28, 2026, with public comments due by June 29, 2026. The guidance addresses disposal pathways including landfilling, underground injection, and thermal treatment for PFAS-containing materials.

headline: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center partners with PTTGC to convert used cooking oil into SAF under 'From Kitchen to Creation' initiative
summary: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center launched the 'From Kitchen to Creation' initiative with PTT Global Chemical, collecting used cooking oil from on-site food operations and converting it into SAF, diverting over 68,000 kilograms of food waste and UCO from landfill in 2025.

headline: Loyola University's lab turns used cooking oil into fuel to run buses
summary: Article profiles Loyola University's Searle Biodiesel Lab, which converts used cooking oil collected from Chicago-area restaurants and institutional sources into biodiesel fuel. Green Grease, the local UCO collector, expects to recycle 1 million gallons in 2026.

headline: Weirton wastewater plant upgrade nears completion
summary: Weirton Sanitary Board declared a $38 million wastewater treatment plant expansion project substantially complete, which doubled treatment capacity from 4 MGD to 8 MGD. Final payments are expected in late May 2026.

headline: Weirton Wastewater Plant Upgrade Nears Completion at 96%
summary: Weirton's $38 million wastewater treatment plant upgrade project has reached 96% completion, designed to expand treatment capacity from 4 to 8 MGD. Final payments are expected in late May. The project was triggered by interest from a large manufacturing company looking to locate in the city.

headline: LJP Waste Solutions Acquires United Liquid Waste Recycling
summary: GreyLion Capital-backed LJP Waste Solutions acquires United Liquid Waste Recycling, materially expanding its liquid-waste footprint across Wisconsin and the upper Midwest. First add-on of size for LJP's liquid-waste line and a notable consolidation move outside the named Big-4 platforms.

headline: Q1 2026 Biodiesel Prices and UCO Feedstock Markets Show Seasonal Volatility
summary: Biodiesel prices in Europe reached $1.50/KG in March 2026, with downward pricing movement of 2.0% between December and March. Europe's shift toward waste-based sources like used cooking oil and animal fats created cost pressure, with limited UCO availability supporting higher prices despite increased U.S. exports.

headline: Folly Beach Considers Water and Sewer Fee Increase
summary: Folly Beach City Council considered increasing water and sewer tap and impact fees after a 5-year rate study revealed they were lower than surrounding areas. The ¾-inch water tap and impact fee would increase from $1,375 to $3,500.

headline: Water Sector Groups Press Congress on Funding, PFAS and Affordability During Water Week
summary: Water sector professionals including the Water Environment Federation held meetings with lawmakers during the annual National Water Policy Fly-In in Washington, D.C. Key topics included declining federal water infrastructure investment, PFAS management compliance costs, and the need for reauthorization of Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds.

headline: Driver shortage causing workforce challenges for Roanoke's Solid Waste Management team
summary: The nationwide demand for CDL drivers is creating workforce challenges for Roanoke's Solid Waste Management operations, forcing temporary suspension of recycling services. The city is implementing crew prioritization and developing drop-off sites as interim solutions.

headline: Ara Partners Announces Up to $500 Million Investment in Sedron to Scale Waste Upcycling Technology
summary: Ara Partners, a global PE and infrastructure firm, announced up to $500 million investment in Sedron Technologies to scale its Varcor® technology, which transforms liquid waste streams including biosolids and agricultural manure into reusable water and fertilizer products. Sedron recently announced a strategic partnership with Synagro for a biosolids upcycling facility in Indiantown, Florida, with construction expected to commence spring 2026 and commissioning in 2028.

headline: New Jersey Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Updated Manifest and Violation Penalties
summary: New Jersey enforces strict manifest requirements and civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation per day for missing or fraudulent manifests. Multiple search results from April 2026 confirm continued enforcement of grease trap regulations across municipalities.

headline: Tierra Environmental & Industrial Brings Expanded Waste Solutions to Chicagoland
summary: Tierra Environmental & Industrial, an IEPA-licensed special waste hauler, has expanded operations into the Chicagoland area. The company delivers professional grease trap cleaning, waste management, and industrial cleaning services, with expertise in managing FOG from commercial kitchens and support for regulatory compliance in the Midwest.

headline: 2026 Requirements for Renewable Fuel Producers in State Clean Fuel Programs
summary: California, Oregon, and Washington now require supply-chain attestations for used cooking oil, animal fats, and corn oil feedstocks starting 2026. New Mexico's Clean Fuel Standard begins April 1, 2026. Compliance focuses on feedstock documentation, land-use records, and transparency for UCO and waste grease sources.

headline: Goldman Sachs-backed LES Acquires New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning
summary: LES continues add-on acquisition strategy under Goldman Sachs ownership, adding a New Orleans-based grease trap cleaning operation to its network.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Acquires New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning
summary: Irving, Texas-based Liquid Environmental Solutions (LES) acquired New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning (NOL), a grease trap and used cooking oil cleaning services provider. Founded in New Orleans in 2015, NOL will be added to LES' network of nonhazardous wastewater collection facilities.

headline: CARB posts new Frequently Asked Questions for 2025 LCFS amendments
summary: CARB released new FAQs clarifying implementation of 2025 LCFS amendments, which include a 20% cap on virgin soybean and canola oil usage, directing producers toward waste-based UCO and grease feedstocks for biodiesel and renewable diesel production.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Makes New Orleans Acquisition
summary: LES acquired New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning (NOL), a grease trap and used cooking oil cleaning services provider based in New Orleans. The acquisition expands LES' network of nonhazardous wastewater collection facilities. LES has executed a series of strategic acquisitions including Grease Masters in December 2025.

headline: DeKalb County FOG Program Reduces SSO Causation from 57% to 52% via Enhanced Inspections
summary: In DeKalb County, Georgia, FOG was responsible for 57% of SSOs in 2014; thanks to efforts of the county's FOG inspectors, this figure dropped to under 52%. All FSEs in DeKalb County must have a Grease Control Device with 30-90 day cleaning cycle using licensed hauler.

headline: GFL Environmental Proposes Acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure
summary: GFL Environmental announced a proposed acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure to strengthen its operations in Western Canada. SECURE's revenue in 2026 is expected to be 1.5 to 1.6 billion.

headline: Meridian Waste acquires Waste Knot, LLC
summary: Meridian Waste Virginia acquired Waste Knot, LLC effective April 1, 2026, strengthening its footprint in the Richmond market. The transaction increases route density and drives volume to the company's vertically integrated MRF and landfill assets.

headline: EPA Finalizes Record-High 2026–2027 Renewable Fuel Standard Volume Obligations
summary: EPA established all-time-high renewable volume obligations for 2026 and 2027, increasing total renewable fuel requirements to 25.82 billion RINs in 2026 and 25.98 billion RINs in 2027. The rule reallocates 70% of small refinery exemption volumes from 2023–2025 into future years and defers the 50% import-related RIN reduction until 2028.

headline: Clean Harbors Issues PFAS Disposal and Treatment Guidance Standards
summary: Clean Harbors released its PFAS management framework in early April, providing an end-to-end cost-effective solution for PFAS in multiple forms and concentrations. The company generated more than $120 million in PFAS-related revenue in 2025, with a pipeline growing about 20% and now seeing growth in the 25% to 35% range for 2026.

headline: EPA Finalizes Historic 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard with Record-High Volumes
summary: The EPA finalized the 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard with all-time-high renewable volume obligations of 25.82 billion RINs in 2026 and 25.98 billion RINs in 2027, including 70% reallocation of small refinery exemptions. Biomass-based diesel nearly doubles to 8.86 billion RINs in 2026, directly supporting renewable diesel and biodiesel producers using waste-based feedstocks like UCO.

headline: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2026 and 2027, Partial Waiver of 2025 Cellulosic Biofuel Volume Requirement
summary: EPA establishes RFS volume requirements for 2026-2027 for biomass-based diesel and advanced biofuel. Final volumes reflect projected growth in feedstocks including used cooking oil (UCO) and animal fats, with sustained emphasis on greenhouse gas reduction.

headline: EPA Finalizes Historic Renewable Fuel Standards for 2026 and 2027 at Record-High Volumes
summary: EPA finalized the RFS "Set 2" rule establishing the highest renewable fuel volume requirements in program history for 2026 and 2027, with 25.82 billion RINs in 2026 and 25.98 billion in 2027. The rule reallocates 70% of small refinery exemptions for 2023-2025 and removes renewable electricity from the program.

headline: U.S. Diesel Prices Spike to $5.40/Gallon Following Middle East Supply Disruptions
source: U.S. Energy Information Administration / Quarterly Update
summary: On March 30, the U.S. average retail diesel price of $5.40/gal was the highest in real terms in over two years, following supply disruptions tied to Middle East military action.

headline: Miller Environmental Group completes acquisitions of Haz-Mat Environmental Services and Canco
summary: Miller Environmental Group, a Coalesce Capital portfolio company, completed acquisitions of Haz-Mat Environmental Services and Canco, expanding its industrial waste treatment and disposal capabilities.

headline: 2026 International Day of Zero Waste Focuses on Food Waste Prevention – Global ESG Momentum Builds
summary: UNEP shifts global narrative on food waste from consumer behavior issue to systems-level ESG priority. Recognition of food loss/waste as central to sustainable consumption, biodiversity, pollution reduction, and climate change. Emphasizes governance structures and public-private partnerships to scale solutions.

headline: Water Infrastructure Grants in 2026: CWSRF, IIJA Programs, and USDA Funding for Clean Water Projects
summary: Federal water infrastructure funding in 2026 totals billions through EPA's Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds, with IIJA authorization running through FY2026. States are actively seeking projects to obligate remaining funds before the authorization window closes.

headline: Wind River Environmental Acquires East Coast Resources
summary: Wind River Environmental acquired East Coast Resources, a Fuquay Varina-based company specializing in grease trap pumping. The deal expands Wind River's footprint in North Carolina and continues its consolidation strategy.

headline: EPA Authorizes Local FOG Ordinances via Clean Water Act NPDES Framework
summary: EPA's Clean Water Act regulations authorize municipalities to require grease interceptors as part of local pretreatment programs, with compliance depending on jurisdiction-specific FOG ordinances. Unpermitted FOG discharge can result in municipal citations with penalties ranging from $500 to $5,000 per violation.

headline: Illinois Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Chicago FOG Program Enforcement Update
summary: Illinois regulations require grease trap cleaning every 90 days minimum with penalties starting at $500 and escalating to $10,000 for repeat violations. The Metropolitan Water Reclamation District (MWRDGC) enforces FOG compliance across Chicago and 128 suburban communities.

headline: Colorado Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Denver and Fort Collins FOG Control Mandates
summary: Colorado Water Quality Control Division oversees FOG pretreatment regulations with local enforcement in Denver, Colorado Springs, Aurora, and Fort Collins. The state mandates 25-33% capacity rules and quarterly to monthly cleaning frequencies.

headline: North Carolina Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Charlotte Water FlowFree Program Expansion
summary: North Carolina municipalities including Charlotte, Raleigh, Durham, and Greensboro enforce FOG regulations with violations ranging from $250 to $1,000+. Charlotte Water's free FlowFree program allows restaurants to submit maintenance documents directly online.

headline: Massachusetts Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — MWRA and Boston Compliance Requirements
summary: Massachusetts mandates 1,000-gallon minimum capacity and 4-foot depth grease traps. Municipal penalties range from $25–$200 per day. The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers enforces code 310 Mass. Reg. 15.230 specifications.

headline: EPA Announces Final 2026-2027 RFS Volumes with 70% Reallocation of Small Refinery Exemptions
summary: EPA announced final 2026-2027 RFS volumes at the highest levels in program history, with record renewable fuel requirements. The agency reallocated 70% of exempted volumes from 2023-2025, eliminating renewable electricity (eRINs) from the program and deferring a 50% RIN reduction on imported fuels until 2028.

headline: Update on the 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard Biofuels Mandate
summary: Analysis of EPA's final 2026-2027 RFS volumes announcing record-high requirements with biomass-based diesel nearly doubling from 2025 levels. The rule includes projections of 41.9 billion gallons of renewable fuel supply growth over two years.

headline: Georgia Oak Partners Acquires Septic Blue
summary: Private equity sponsor Georgia Oak Partners acquired Septic Blue, a Southeast regional leader in septic tank services operating in Atlanta, Charlotte, and Raleigh metro areas. Source Capital provided debt financing and equity co-investment.

headline: Barrel Energy Inc. (OTC: BRLL) Acquires Renewable Energy Company Happy Traps to Expand Waste-to-Energy Platform
summary: Barrel Energy acquired Happy Traps, a Portland, Maine waste-to-energy and environmental services company, which has 200+ recurring commercial clients and >3,500 grease trap cleanings with customer retention above 95%, positioning Barrel Energy to expand its grease-management services into the $8+ billion U.S. market.

headline: Waste Hauling Insurance: Why Recycling & Garbage Companies Are Getting Hit at Renewal
summary: Waste and recycling haulers face increased exposure and liability challenges securing adequate insurance coverage. The sector is experiencing difficult renewal conditions as companies navigate complex risk profiles across diverse operations.

headline: Wind River Environmental Acquires J&M Transfer, Inc.
summary: Wind River continues aggressive expansion, acquiring J&M Transfer to extend its liquid waste transfer capabilities.

headline: Miami-Dade Grease Trap Compliance for Restaurants 2026 — Federal Consent Decree Enforcement Remains Strict
summary: Miami-Dade enforces FOG compliance under a federal consent decree with 90-day cleaning maximums and 99% efficiency requirements. A February 2026 County Commission resolution signals potential future relief, though current regulations remain fully enforceable.

headline: CDL rule affecting non-citizens taking effect despite waste hauler concerns
summary: A federal CDL eligibility rule restricting non-domiciled drivers took effect March 16, 2026, immediately affecting up to 20% of Waste Pro's drivers in Southwest Florida. The regulation impacts asylum seekers, refugees, and DACA recipients previously eligible for commercial licenses, exacerbating existing driver shortages.

headline: LCFS 2024 Amendments: Tightened CI Targets and Expanded Verification Framework
summary: California's 2024 LCFS amendments, effective July 1, 2025, significantly tightened credit supply and expanded producer obligations. The 2025 reporting year required GREET 4.0 model use, and 2026 brings expanded feedstock and land-use documentation for renewable fuels from waste oils including UCO.

headline: Junk Removal Business Insurance Cost (2026 Rates)
summary: Broad waste/junk removal insurance survey noting that disposal fees and regional regulations significantly affect both operations and risk exposure for hauling businesses.

headline: FMCSA CDL Rule Restricting Non-Domiciled Drivers Takes Effect; Waste Haulers Face 20% Driver Impact
summary: FMCSA final rule affecting CDL eligibility for nearly 200,000 drivers took effect, restricting certain non-domiciled drivers including asylum seekers and refugees from holding CDLs. Waste Pro reports the rule change would affect up to 20% of its drivers in Southwest Florida, delaying service and making it hard to replace qualified drivers.

headline: Quatra Secures 15-Year Used Cooking Oil Supply Agreement with TotalEnergies
source: Coherent Market Insights / Used Cooking Oil Market Report
summary: Quatra signed a 15-year agreement to supply TotalEnergies with 60,000 tons of European used cooking oil annually from 2026, to be processed into biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel.

headline: CDL Immigration Rule Impact: Federal Rules Bar Asylum Seekers from Commercial Driving
summary: Federal rules implemented in March 2026 now bar asylum seekers, refugees, and DACA recipients from obtaining or renewing CDLs, with an estimated 200,000 active CDL holders—roughly 5% of all commercial drivers—directly affected. Texas is the epicenter of the driver shortage impact due to its high freight volume and disproportionate immigrant driver population.

headline: EPA Draft Guidance 2026: Chemical/Biological FOG Treatment Does Not Satisfy Clean Water Act 'Removal' Standards
summary: The EPA's 2026 draft guidance explicitly prohibits enzyme or biological additives as FOG treatment substitutes, stating they do not constitute 'removal' under Clean Water Act standards. Municipalities are adopting ordinances voiding permits for establishments using additives.

headline: The Future of FOG Compliance: What's Coming in 2027 and Beyond
summary: EPA's draft 2026 guidance clarifies that chemical or biological FOG treatment does not constitute legal 'removal' under Clean Water Act standards. Water Environment Federation laboratory studies show these products can increase downstream FOG deposits by 30-40%, prompting regulatory bodies and municipalities to enforce mechanical removal as the only defensible compliance strategy.

headline: EPA Draft Guidance: Chemical/Biological FOG Treatment Does Not Constitute 'Removal'
summary: The EPA's draft 2026 guidance clarifies that chemical or biological FOG treatment does not qualify as 'removal' under Clean Water Act standards. Water Environment Federation research shows biological additives can increase downstream FOG deposits by 30-40%, pushing regulatory focus toward mechanical removal and IoT-enabled grease interceptor monitoring.

headline: Seekye Capital Acquires SES Mid Atlantic, Advantage Septic and Joiner Micro Laboratories
summary: Private equity firm Seekye Capital announced its inaugural acquisition creating a comprehensive wastewater and environmental services platform. The deal brings together soil/environmental consulting, septic services, and environmental lab capabilities.

headline: Wind River Environmental acquires Hapchuk, Inc. and Liquid Assets Disposal, Inc.
summary: Wind River Environmental acquired Hapchuk, Inc., a provider of grease and septic pumping in Pennsylvania, and entered into an agreement for sister company Liquid Assets Disposal, Inc., which operates a West Virginia treatment facility for grease, septic, and non-hazardous liquid waste.

headline: Black Box Intelligence: 9% of Full-Service Restaurants at Risk of Closure in 2026
summary: Black Box Intelligence data shows 9% of full-service restaurants are at risk of shuttering, while only 4% of limited-service units could close this year. For the 3% of Full-Service restaurants experiencing sales drop exceeding 50%, the question for 2026 isn't if they will close, but when.

headline: Fats, Oils, and Grease Stormwater Pollution
summary: Municipal FOG pollution prevention page updated with current regulatory and environmental compliance information. Notes EPA estimate that 47% of sewer blockages are due to grease from restaurants and industrial sources.

headline: Raleigh, NC FOG Program Updates – Municipal ESG Compliance & Infrastructure Oversight
source: City of Raleigh, NC Official Website
summary: City of Raleigh updates FOG stormwater pollution program guidance (last updated Feb 3, 2026). Emphasizes EPA estimate that 47% of sewer blockages are FOG-related; reinforces municipal FOG permitting and compliance framework as part of broader ESG infrastructure goals.

headline: Insurance for Waste & Recycle Haulers: Protecting Your Business and Operations
summary: Article discusses rising insurance costs for waste and recycling haulers in 2026, noting increased exposure and liability challenges. Liquid waste haulers are called out as requiring special pollution liability endorsements and additional coverage.

headline: Used Cooking Oil Market Valuation Reaches $8.47B in 2026; Set to Grow to $13.86B by 2033
source: Coherent Market Insights / UCO Market Report
summary: Used Cooking Oil Market valuation is estimated to reach USD 8.47 Bn in 2026 and is anticipated to grow to USD 13.86 Bn by 2033 with steady CAGR of 7.3%. The food service segment is anticipated to account for 46.9% of the UCO market in 2026, with North America leading the global market at 45.2% share.

headline: Food Waste Laws & Regulations in the USA in 2026: ESG Compliance Requirements Tighten
summary: Comprehensive review of 2026 food waste regulations across U.S. states, with emphasis on organics diversion, FOG management compliance, and ESG reporting requirements. California SB 1383 now requires 97% of jurisdictions to operate integrated organics programs; emphasis on waste-to-energy and alternative treatment technologies.

headline: PFAS Behavior During Water and Wastewater Treatment
summary: The Global Waste Management Symposium (GWMS) session on 'PFAS Behavior During Water and Wastewater Treatment' explored mechanics of contaminant management during treatment processes.

headline: Key Food Waste Laws & Regulations in the USA in 2026
summary: Overview of 2026 food waste regulations across U.S. states, with focus on organics diversion and compliance requirements. California's SB 1383 continues to drive industry changes; on-site biodigestion solutions and compliance infrastructure expanding.

headline: Papa John's Announces 200 Restaurant Closures in 2026; 300 Total by End of 2027
summary: Papa John's announced in a February 26 earnings call that it plans to close about 200 restaurants in 2026 as part of broader effort to shut down 300 underperforming locations by end of 2027. Most franchised locations slated for closure are over a decade old, with average unit volume under $600,000 and typically negative four-wall income.

headline: ESG in the Food Industry: Enhancing Transparency and Accountability
summary: Discusses ESG frameworks and standards required in food sector operations, covering environmental footprint, supply-chain sustainability, worker welfare, and food safety. Addresses how food waste reduction fits into ESG compliance strategies for food companies.

headline: Fats, Oils, and Grease (FOG) Management in the Restaurant Sector: A Study of Guadalajara
summary: Peer-reviewed research on FOG management examining collection systems, restaurant practices, and grease trap waste characterization. Emphasizes circular economy approaches and FOG valorization through energy recovery pathways to address environmental sustainability.

headline: Austin Wastewater Plant Expansion Costs to Increase $600M
summary: City officials considered a $600 million (66%) cost increase to the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion project. The total project cost rose to $1.5 billion due to rising costs of goods and services, site constraints, and other factors. The project aims to increase capacity to 100 MGD by 2032.

headline: What to Know About the Section 45Z PTC Proposed Regulations
summary: Treasury and IRS issue proposed regulations for Section 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit covering transportation fuels including biodiesel from used cooking oil. Credit amounts up to $1/gallon for qualifying facilities through 2027, with heightened scrutiny on imported UCO feedstock sourcing.

headline: Average Waste Management CDL Driver Salary Reaches $29.71/Hour; Shortage Persists
source: ZipRecruiter / Hazardous Waste Driver Salary Data
summary: As of May 1, 2026, the average hourly pay for hazardous waste driver in the United States is $28.59; most workers earn between $24.28 and $30.05 per hour depending on experience, location, and employer.

headline: The Water and Wastewater Equipment, Treatment and Transport (WWETT) Show 2026 Celebrates Industry-Leading Innovations and Solutions
summary: The WWETT Show 2026 successfully concluded its Indianapolis edition (Feb 16-19) with a 6% attendance increase over 2025. The expo floor showcased cutting-edge products and solutions including water filtration, robotics, portable systems, and AI-powered dash cams addressing industry's evolving needs.

headline: Clean Harbors Acquires Industrial and Rail Services from Depot Connect International
summary: Clean Harbors acquired the Industrial and Rail Services business from Depot Connect International (DCI).

headline: Depot Connect International Sells Industrial and Rail Services Business to Clean Harbors
summary: Clean Harbors completed an acquisition of industrial and rail services from Depot Connect International as referenced in Q1 2026 earnings announcements, supporting the company's strategic growth in industrial services.

headline: WWETT Show 2026 Concludes with Record Attendance and Industry Innovation
summary: The WWETT Show 2026 successfully concluded February 16-19 at the Indiana Convention Center with a 6% increase in attendance from the 2025 edition. The expo floor featured cutting-edge products including water filtration systems, robotics, portable systems, and AI-powered dash cams, with education tracks covering pipe lining, sewer relining, and portable sanitation.

headline: Valorization of used cooking oil: challenges, current developments, life cycle assessment and future prospects
summary: Academic review examining global UCO recycling landscape with annual production of 41-67 million tons. Explores waste-to-value pathways including biodiesel, bioasphalt, and biopolymers; notes only 10-20% of food service UCO is currently collected for recycling.

headline: City of Stanton RFP for Environmental Services for NPDES and FOG Programs
summary: The City of Stanton is requesting proposals from qualified consultants to provide services for National Pollutant Elimination Systems (NPDES) and Fats Oils & Grease (FOG) programs with question deadline March 11, 2026.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Acquires Commercial Pumping Services
summary: Liquid Environmental Solutions has acquired Commercial Pumping Services, a leading provider of grease trap and used cooking oil collection services. Based in St. Charles County, MO and founded in 2000, Commercial Pumping Services will be added to LES' extensive network of non-hazardous wastewater collection facilities.

headline: Darling Ingredients Q4 Earnings Call Highlights
summary: Darling Ingredients closed fiscal 2025 with Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $336.1M. Management highlighted improving policy backdrop for renewable fuels heading into 2026, with executives pointing to strengthened U.S. Renewable Volume Obligation as a major swing factor for Diamond Green Diesel operations.

headline: Sustainable transformation of waste cooking oil: A global review of valorization pathways and future directions
summary: Comprehensive review of WCO conversion technologies (2019-2025), highlighting biodiesel production efficiencies of 87-96% and emerging applications in bio-jet fuels, bio-asphalt, and biopolymers. Identifies need for next-generation catalysts and machine learning optimization.

headline: Noodles & Company Closing 30-35 Additional U.S. Restaurants in 2026
source: Mashed / Popular Restaurant Chains Closing Locations 2026
summary: Noodles & Company announced plans to close between 30 and 35 additional restaurants across the United States in 2026 after closing 33 company-owned and nine franchise locations in 2025.

headline: IoT Smart Sensors Become Essential for Grease Trap Compliance and Cost Savings in 2026
summary: In 2026, the smartest way to lower grease trap installation costs long-term is by spending an extra $250 – $450 upfront on IoT smart sensors. Data shows that IoT-enabled kitchens face almost zero emergency shutdowns compared to manual setups, and many 2026 commercial insurers offer a 5–10% discount on property insurance if you prove continuous digital monitoring of waste lines.

headline: Grease Trap Installation Costs 2026: 11 Smart Ways to Save $4,000+
summary: 2026 market analysis of IoT-enabled smart sensors ($250-$450) for grease traps with municipal FOG (Fats, Oils, Grease, and Solids) program requirements, digital permitting, and insurance premium discounts (5-10%) for continuous digital monitoring compliance.

headline: Unique ESG Considerations for the Waste Industry – Including Liquid Waste & FOG Management
summary: Analysis of ESG frameworks for waste management operations, including specific guidance on GHG emissions disclosure (particularly methane from landfilled grease), fleet efficiency, and SASB/GRI reporting standards. Highlights how FOG-related operations must integrate climate risk and sustainability metrics.

headline: EPA National Pretreatment Program — Regulatory History Updated with Current Rulemaking Activities
summary: EPA updated pretreatment program regulatory history on February 3, 2026, noting current rulemaking activities affecting 40 CFR Part 403. Activities include Effluent Limitation Guidelines for dental and oil/gas industries.

headline: Global Food Waste Supply Chain Costs to Reach $540B in 2026 – Business Case for ESG-Driven Waste Solutions
summary: Avery Dennison research confirms food waste will cost global supply chain $540B in 2026. 72% of supply chain leaders cite meat waste as greatest challenge; over 70% of business leaders see waste reduction as growth opportunity. Report positions circular economy and ESG as business imperatives, not just compliance requirements.

headline: Governor Hochul Announces $288 Million to Make Local Water Infrastructure Projects Affordable
summary: New York State announced $288 million in grants and low-cost financing for local water infrastructure projects as part of Governor Hochul's $3.75 billion five-year plan. Funding supports wastewater system improvements, lead service line replacement, and lead pipe remediation.

headline: Governor Hochul Announces $288 Million in Water Infrastructure Funding
summary: Governor Hochul announced $288 million in grants and low-cost financing for water infrastructure projects, part of a landmark $3.75 billion plan. Funding includes IIJA grants and state resources for lead service line replacement, modernization of aging systems, and wastewater improvements across New York communities.

headline: CDL Truck Driver Shortage Continues; Carriers Offer Higher Pay and Flexible Benefits
source: America Truck Driving / Truck Driver Shortage in 2026
summary: One of the most noticeable impacts of the driver shortage in 2026 is improved compensation, with many carriers offering higher starting pay, sign-on bonuses, tuition reimbursement, and flexible scheduling options.

headline: NYC Grease Trap Cleaning Guide — DEP Requirements and Best Practices Updated for 2026
summary: New York City DEP enforces maximum $10,000 per day penalties for FOG violations, with cleaning every 1-3 months required. The 25% capacity rule remains the primary enforcement threshold for the nation's strictest FOG program.

headline: Tipping Fee Increase at Columbia-Shuswap Refuse Facilities
summary: Refuse disposal tipping fees increased from $90 to $100 per ton, while mixed loads without recyclables removed increased to $350 per ton from $270. The increases address operational cost pressures in the regional waste management system.

headline: Solid Waste Collection Industry Will Add 14,200 Collection Driver Jobs by 2026
summary: By 2026, the solid waste collection industry will have 14,200 new jobs for collection drivers and riders; 1,900 new jobs for diesel service technicians and mechanics; and 300 new jobs for welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers.

headline: Grease Trap Monitoring Platforms Scale to Enterprise Portfolio Management
summary: Ultrasonic level sensors provide non-contact measurement of grease layer thickness and overall fill levels without requiring components that contact grease directly, providing reliable measurement requiring minimal maintenance compared to contact-based alternatives. Cloud-based platforms aggregate data from multiple grease traps into unified dashboards, enabling centralized management that scales from single locations to enterprise portfolios efficiently.

headline: Grease Trap Monitoring: Prevent Costly Overflows Guide 2026
summary: 2026 grease trap monitoring strategies using ultrasonic level sensors, battery-powered cellular sensors, and cloud-based platforms providing facility-wide visibility with automated alerting for service threshold management.

headline: UCO Supply-Demand Imbalance Continues: Global Collection Falls Short of Biofuel Targets
summary: Fastmarkets estimates total UCO usage in the US in 2024 at 8.4 billion pounds (42% increase), but UCO collection is estimated at only 3.3 billion pounds in 2024, insufficient to meet the biofuel industry's demand for 5.7 billion pounds of feedstock. Global UCO supply is expected to grow, fueled by improved collection efficiency and investments by biofuel producers integrating upstream into the waste oil value chain.

headline: Chinese UCO Export Tariffs Reshape Global Biofuel Feedstock Trade Flows and Pricing
summary: U.S. farmers welcome trade protection as soy oil prices and demand are expected to firm up as domestic feedstocks replace lost Chinese UCO, and U.S. renewable diesel plants may need to pivot to relying more on homegrown oils and other waste fats. Chinese suppliers are now pivoting to Europe and other Asian countries to offset the loss of the U.S. market.

headline: United Site Services Chapter 11 Filing
summary: United Site Services filed for Chapter 11 protection on December 29, 2025, reporting $1-10 billion in assets and liabilities. The company provides non-hazardous liquid waste services including grease trap waste removal.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Acquired by Goldman Sachs Infrastructure Fund
source: Multiple (ESG Today, Baird, Simpson Thacher, Audax)
summary: Goldman Sachs Alternatives announced an agreement by its infrastructure team to acquire non-hazardous liquid waste management services provider Liquid Environmental Solutions (LES), from Boston-based investor Audax Private Equity. Audax had acquired the company in Q4 2017 and executed a Buy & Build strategy, nearly doubling the company's footprint to over 90 locations across 50 states; LES executed 13 acquisitions that helped drive geographic growth and entry into adjacent services.

headline: GFL Environmental Closes Frontier Waste Solutions Acquisition in Texas
summary: GFL completed Frontier Waste Solutions acquisition in early April as a leading vertically integrated solid waste business across the Texas Triangle. The company completed eight acquisitions since the start of the year, adding an estimated $425 million to $450 million in annualized revenue.

headline: Renewable Diesel Feedstock Competition Intensifies: UCO Policy Incentives Drive Market Volatility
summary: Global collectable UCO volumes in 2030 may realistically reach 8–12 million tonnes/year, supporting 15–22 million tonnes/year of SAF and renewable diesel combined, yet net-zero-aligned roadmaps envision aviation SAF demand of 60–120 million tonnes/year by 2035, creating structural feedstock tension. There is intense competition between biodiesel, renewable diesel, and SAF producers for a limited pool of UCO.

headline: Used Cooking Oil (UCO) Price Forecast: A Cornerstone Feedstock for Sustainable Aviation Fuel
summary: Fastmarkets analysis of UCO market dynamics showing 2024 US UCO usage reached 8.4 billion pounds (42% increase), but collection at only 3.3 billion pounds falls short of the industry's demand for 5.7 billion pounds, creating significant feedstock supply constraints.

headline: LES Acquires Grease Masters in St. Louis
summary: Goldman-backed LES acquires St. Louis-based Grease Masters, a grease trap, UCO, drain cleaning, and kitchen exhaust hood cleaning provider.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Acquires Grease Masters
summary: In December 2025, LES acquired St. Louis-based Grease Masters, a grease trap/commercial drain line cleaning, used cooking oil, and kitchen exhaust hood cleaning provider, expanding LES's Midwest footprint.

headline: [Date unverified] Regulatory Update: Iowa EPA FCG Program Developments and Clean Water Standards
summary: Unpermitted FOG discharge can result in municipal citations with penalties ranging from $500 to $5,000 per violation, mandatory equipment installation, increased inspection frequency, and cost recovery if discharge causes infrastructure damage. The Clean Water Act authorizes civil penalties up to $59,973 per violation per day for unpermitted discharges.

headline: [Date unverified] WEFTEC 2026 Conference Scheduled for New Orleans
summary: WEFTEC 2026, the Water Environment Federation's 99th Annual Technical Exhibition and Conference, is scheduled for September 26-30 at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center in New Orleans. The event will feature water quality education, networking opportunities, and cutting-edge solutions for wastewater and environmental professionals.

headline: [Date unverified] Kitchen Carbon Offsets: What §45Z Makes Your Grease Worth – Federal Tax Credits Transform Used Cooking Oil Finance
summary: Article analyzes how the Inflation Reduction Act's §45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit creates federal tax incentives (up to $0.70/gal) for low-carbon biodiesel from recycled cooking oil. California alone could unlock ~$32M in annual credit value; the three-year credit window runs through 2027 before sunsetting.
